one_liner: Pure-Rust port of the Oniguruma regex engine and the vscode-oniguruma scanner; about 2.2x faster than C Oniguruma on everyday searches and 12x on TextMate highlighting replays.
what_it_does: Ferroni is a line-by-line Rust port of Oniguruma's parser, compiler, optimizer and backtracking VM. It covers the full Oniguruma syntax (look-around, backreferences, conditionals, absent expressions, subexpression calls, 12 syntax modes, Unicode 18.0) for ASCII and UTF-8 subjects. It exposes two APIs: an idiomatic one (Regex, Captures, match iterators, plus a Scanner with vscode-oniguruma's multi-pattern find_next_match and UTF-16 offsets), and the original C entry points under their C names (onig_new, onig_search, onig_regset_*). So existing Oniguruma call sites port nearly one to one, but it is a Rust crate, not a C-ABI drop-in library.
how_it_is_fast: The structure of C Oniguruma is kept, and Rust-only search additions are layered on top (ADR-007, ADR-008). Literal prefix scans use memchr, memchr2, memchr3 and a memmem Finder. Alternations of plain literals become literal tries, and RegSet fallback entries are filtered by required literals (Aho-Corasick for several of them). Leading class runs are skipped, which the project credits with 22-31x on email-like scans, and leading checks let the search jump ahead. Unicode classes use a binary range lookup and adjacent ASCII class runs are batched. Scanner searches use a first-byte dispatch table, rejects on the first instruction, and a lazy-DFA pre-filter built on regex-automata (the default 'dfa-prefilter' feature) plus result and pattern caches. The large highlighting margin comes mostly from these RegSet additions measured against vscode-oniguruma's onig_regset_search(ONIG_REGSET_POSITION_LEAD), not from Rust codegen.
when_to_use: TextMate-grammar syntax highlighting or tokenizing in Rust (a Shiki or vscode-textmate equivalent): the scanner replays of real Shiki calls for the C, Java and PHP grammars ran 8.5-17.6x faster than the vscode-oniguruma C scanner.
Replacing a C Oniguruma dependency (via the onig crate or FFI) to drop the C toolchain and C memory-safety exposure, when your subjects are UTF-8 or ASCII.
Patterns the regex crate cannot express (look-behind, backreferences, possessive and atomic groups, \G, recursion, absent operator) on search and extraction work over kilobyte-to-megabyte documents.
Untrusted or hostile patterns and input, where per-search time, retry and stack limits plus the compile-time catastrophic-backtracking check matter.
when_not_to_use: Patterns that fit the regex crate: regex was 1.5x faster on the everyday set and guarantees linear time; PCRE2 JIT was 2.1x faster on everyday and 3.5x faster on advanced patterns among the tasks it could run.

Workloads dominated by compiling patterns, such as one-shot highlighting of a short snippet: C Oniguruma compiled some grammars 2-3x faster (ts_279_compile 0.53, rust_81_compile 0.35 on EPYC), and some single tasks still favour C (rfc5322_emails 0.67, ipv6_addresses 0.64 on EPYC).
Non-UTF-8 encodings (27 of Oniguruma's 29 are not ported, e.g. PHP mbregex with EUC-JP or Shift_JIS) or code that needs the POSIX/GNU regcomp/regexec APIs.

Exact error parity on runaway patterns: where a Rust-only filter leaves out an attempt that would have exhausted the retry limit, C reports ONIGERR_RETRY_LIMIT_IN_MATCH_OVER and Ferroni returns the next match or no match (ADR-008). Ferroni also accepts \x{140000}-\x{1FFFFF}, which C rejects.

Conservative production use: 9 stars and very fast churn (2.0.0 with breaking changes on 2026-10-09, 2.1.0 and 2.1.1 within two days). It also had recent parity bugs on malformed UTF-8 (#257, #259, #261) and a stack overflow on deeply nested patterns (#285), all fixed by 2026-10-08.

integration.dependencies: aho-corasick, bitflags, memchr, smallvec; with the default 'dfa-prefilter' feature also regex-automata and regex-syntax. A C compiler is needed only for the 'ffi'/'onigmo' benchmark features.
integration.platforms: any Rust target; memchr's SIMD paths are used where available (SSE2/AVX2 on x86-64, NEON on aarch64); measured on Linux x86-64 and macOS arm64
integration.thread_safety: Regex is Send + Sync and cheap to Clone (clones share one compiled program); Scanner is Send + Sync but its search takes &mut self, so each thread needs its own scanner. Limits can be set process-wide or per search.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: it keeps the Oniguruma C API names and semantics (all 2,974 upstream UTF-8 test cases pass) and a vscode-oniguruma-shaped Scanner, but only as a Rust crate (no C ABI), for UTF-8 and ASCII only, without the POSIX/GNU APIs, and with small documented differences in retry-limit errors.

gotchas: The speed-up does not come from Rust codegen. The everyday and advanced figures depend on Rust-only search filters, and the 12x highlighting figure depends on the RegSet dispatch, required-literal and DFA pre-filter additions against the vscode-oniguruma C scanner's ONIG_REGSET_POSITION_LEAD search. Disabling the default 'dfa-prefilter' feature gives up part of the scanner gain.

The harness is symmetric where it matters. Ferroni and C both go through onig_search with a reused region (benches/general_regex.rs, regex_tasks.rs). In the replays both get fresh string-cache identities every iteration (corpus.strings() vs CReplay::fresh_ids()), and the C side converts UTF-16 starts to byte offsets outside the timing. One residual asymmetry: each side's scanners persist across Criterion iterations, so Ferroni's lazy DFA pre-filter is always warm, and its build cost is not in the replay timing.

The pre-filter can backfire. In the earlier run 37989957431 the flat CSS scanner regressed to 11-16 ms (C 4.8x faster) until PR #324 retired the pre-filter on sets whose DFA cache thrashes. Issue #327 (warm JSON and Astro regressions in Ferriki under 2.0.0) was fixed in 2.1.0 by building the pre-filter only after a warm-up. The published textmate set covers only the C, C++, Java, PHP and SCSS replays and the three battle_bench grammars (TypeScript, CSS, Rust); the JSON and Astro replays that regressed are not in it.

The default nesting limit dropped to 256 units (128 groups) in 2.0.0, so deeply nested patterns now fail with ParseDepthLimitOver unless onig_set_parse_depth_limit and onig_set_ast_node_limit are both raised.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Ferroni over the regex crate only when you need Oniguruma syntax (look-around, backreferences, TextMate grammars) or the vscode-oniguruma scanner; for plain search, regex is faster and linear-time. mojo-regex targets Python re and Rust regex syntax in Mojo, not Oniguruma.
verified_claims_summary: Author-run Criterion means (30 samples) on Blacksmith CI runners on 2026-10-09: an Apple M4 Pro (virtual, macOS 26.3) and an unnamed AMD EPYC with AVX-512 (Ubuntu 24.04). Ferroni was built with rustc 1.99.0 and thin LTO; C Oniguruma (pinned commit f95747b) was built at -O3 by GCC 13.3.0 or Apple clang 21.0.0, and the vscode-oniguruma C scanner was used for the replays. Every engine was validated against C's matches before timing. Geomean over both hosts: 2.2x faster than C on 32 everyday tasks (2.12x EPYC, 2.39x M4 Pro), 1.4x on 17 advanced tasks, and about 12x on the C, Java and PHP Shiki replays (8.5-17.6x per document).
status_note: Active (2.1.1 released 2026-10-11, about 6.5k crates.io downloads), BSD-2-Clause like upstream, and declared feature-complete with maintenance-only plans now that C Oniguruma ended in April 2025. The benchmark evidence is unusually complete (raw measurements.json, SHA256SUMS, ADRs), but the project is young, single-vendor and has 9 stars.
